answer: Sybil resistance via quota auctions. Each epoch only K=200 new identities are admitted by sealed bid; a bid is valid only with a 1 GB memory-hard proof over the fixed Mesa table, priced per bid, so cost never amortizes across puppets. A randomness beacon picks the quorum that opens bids and seals the round as a signed 14-field record (a sonnet) anchoring the epoch; state rejects admissions beyond K. Buying n puppets costs n 1 GB proofs plus n clearing bids, and the global quota caps issuance speed, so marginal cost grows at least linearly in n; honest users bid once.
